ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an operational amplifier negative-feedback circuit. The input voltage ui is connected to the inverting input through resistor R1; the feedback resistor Rf is connected back from the output terminal uo to the inverting input, forming negative feedback. In the figure, the non-inverting input was originally grounded through R2. The problem states that this ground reference of the non-inverting terminal should be changed to a 5 V power supply. Reasoning: Under negative feedback, an ideal op amp satisfies v- = v+, and the input terminal current is 0. Since the non-inverting terminal is connected to 5 V, the inverting terminal voltage v- = 5 V. Write KCL at the inverting input node: the current flowing from the input terminal through R1 into this node is equal to the current flowing through Rf toward the output terminal, namely (ui - 5)/R1 = (5 - uo)/Rf. Substitute ui = 10 V, R1 = 10 kΩ, Rf = 20 kΩ: (10 - 5)/10k = (5 - uo)/20k. Solving gives 5 - uo = 10, so uo = -5 V.
